subject.title: refactor(ui): use Web Awesome controls throughout Control UI

question: After the wizard blocker is repaired and real browser evidence is supplied, should OpenClaw accept Web Awesome 3.10.0 as the Control UI composite-control owner together with the higher startup JavaScript budgets?
rationale: The permanent third-party control dependency and startup-budget tradeoff are product and maintenance choices that tests cannot authorize, and the protected `maintainer` label requires explicit human handling.

options.title: Repair, prove, then accept
options.body: Fix preselected wizard submission, add real keyboard and mobile-touch proof, then accept the dependency and budget increase if the observed UX is sound.

options.title: Narrow the migration
options.body: Land only the highest-value dialog, menu, and tab replacements while retaining native or existing controls where dependency cost or touch behavior is not yet justified.

options.title: Pause the dependency adoption
options.body: Keep the merged accessibility foundation and defer Web Awesome until its runtime cost and mobile interaction behavior have stronger evidence.

recommendation.title: Repair, prove, then accept
recommendation.body: Fix preselected wizard submission, add real keyboard and mobile-touch proof, then accept the dependency and budget increase if the observed UX is sound.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history shows ownership of both the merged accessibility foundation and this dependency migration.
